defaults.permitted_development: Across Devon, detached domestic garages are usually easiest on the planning permission route when they stay clearly secondary to the house, respect height and boundary relationships, and avoid creating a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. Visible frontages and more open plots can make roof form, materials and street impact more sensitive than a simple garage sketch suggests.

rules.height_rules: Garage proposals across Devon are normally judged first on overall height, eaves height and whether the roof form keeps the building subordinate to the main house.
rules.depth_rules: Garage footprint and siting across Devon are usually easiest where the building stays clearly ancillary, fits comfortably within the plot and does not take over the frontage or usable garden. The route normally gets harder once the garage starts to dominate site coverage or read as a second main structure.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour relationship and vehicle access are the recurring pressure points for garages in Devon, especially where a new crossover or tight turning arrangement is involved.
rules.roof_rules: Low-profile garage roofs are generally easier than taller roof forms that create storage volume, apparent accommodation or a more dominant outbuilding shape.
rules.materials_rules: Garages are normally easiest to support when the materials, door treatment and overall appearance sit comfortably with the house and local street scene.

rules.permitted_development: In East Devon, a detached garage is usually easiest to keep off the formal planning permission route when it remains clearly secondary to the house, sits comfortably within the plot and does not create a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. The answer usually gets harder when the garage is pushed forward in the plot and starts to compete with the house on the street frontage.

rules.height_rules: In East Devon, garage height is usually the first measurement to sense-check, especially where the building sits close to a boundary or uses a taller pitched roof.
rules.depth_rules: A garage in East Devon is more likely to need a closer review if the footprint starts to dominate the garden or front part of the site rather than sitting as a modest supporting structure.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour impact and highway practicality all matter in East Devon, particularly if the garage depends on a new or altered vehicle access.
rules.roof_rules: Garage roofs in East Devon are usually easiest where they stay low-profile and do not suggest loft storage, accommodation or a second-storey form.
rules.materials_rules: Materials and frontage treatment should help the garage read as a subordinate domestic building in East Devon, not as a visually dominant addition to the property.

restrictions.conservation_area: Garages in conservation areas within East Devon often receive a closer design review where they affect the character of a visible frontage or the wider street scene.
restrictions.listed_building: Garages affecting a listed building or its setting in East Devon usually need a more careful planning and heritage consent check.
